final_answer:
1) EXPAND RIDE-SHARING & CAR-POOLING PROGRAMS  
PROS: REDUCES VEHICLE COUNT, LOWER EMISSIONS, COST-EFFECTIVE.  
CONS: DEPENDENT ON PARTICIPATION, MAY DISPLACE PARKING DEMAND, INITIAL MARKETING CHALLENGES.

2) IMPLEMENT SMART TRAFFIC SIGNALS & AI-POWERED ROUTING  
PROS: OPTIMIZES FLOW IN REAL-TIME, LOW COST PER VEHICLE, IMPROVES SAFETY.  
CONS: HIGH INITIAL TECH COST, POTENTIAL FOR SYSTEM FAILURES, PRIVACY CONCERNS WITH DATA COLLECTION.

3) CREATE MORE WALKABLE COMMUNITIES WITH MIXED-USE ZONING  
PROS: REDUCES NEED FOR LONG COMMUTES, BOOSTS LOCAL ECONOMY, IMPROVES QUALITY OF LIFE.  
CONS: LONG-TERM, CAN INCREASE SHORT-TERM CONSTRUCTION CHAOS, REQUIRES PLANNING AND POLICY ALIGNMENT.

4) INTRODUCE ROAD USAGE CHARGES (CONGESTION TAX) DURING PEAK HOURS  
PROS: DIRECTLY REDUCES PEAK TRAVEL, FUNDS PUBLIC TRANSPORT, CLEAR DISINCENTIVE.  
CONS: PERCEIVED AS REGULATION, MAY DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECT LOW-INCOME DRIVERS, COMPLEX ADMINISTRATION.

5) PROMOTE REMOTE WORK & FLEXIBLE SCHEDULING  
PROS: DRAMATICALLY REDUCES MORNING/EVENING PEAKS, LOW COST, BENEFITS EMPLOYEES.  
CONS: NOT UNIVERSAL (ALL EMPLOYEES CAN’T WORK REMOTELY), MAY REDUCE IN-CITY COMMERCIAL ACTIVITY, NEEDS EMPLOYER BUY-IN.
